Best telescopes under $500

Every scope here costs under $500 — ranked from cheapest to priciest. Under $500 is the sweet spot for a first telescope: enough aperture to show you Saturn's rings and real deep-sky objects, without the regret if you upgrade later.

#1

Celestron AstroMaster 70AZ around $150

The honest $150 start. A real refractor with no collimation — good for the Moon and planets, and cheap enough that it doesn't matter if the hobby doesn't stick.

The classic sub-$200 first refractor.

  • Watch out:
  • 70mm limits deep-sky views
  • Basic mount is wobbly at high power
Read the full pick →

#2

Orion StarBlast 4.5 Astro Reflector around $250

The tabletop Dobsonian classic. More aperture per dollar than cheap refractors, though the mount is basic and it needs something to sit on.

The grab-and-go tabletop that hooks kids and adults alike.

  • Watch out:
  • Needs a sturdy table
  • Fast f/4 mirror needs collimation
Read the full pick →

#3

Sky-Watcher Evostar 102 around $280

A sharp 4-inch achromatic refractor — but it's the optical tube only, so budget a mount and tripod before it fits under $500.

The classic 4-inch achromatic refractor — sharp, simple, honest.

  • Watch out:
  • Optical tube only — needs a mount and tripod
  • Achromatic design shows false color on bright objects
Read the full pick →

#4

Sky-Watcher Heritage 150P around $300

Our sweet-spot pick: 6 inches of Dobsonian that shows Saturn's rings, Jupiter's bands, and hundreds of deep-sky objects.

6 inches of tabletop Dobsonian — the sweet spot starter scope.

  • Watch out:
  • Needs a sturdy table or stool
  • No tracking — planets drift
Read the full pick →

#5

Orion SkyQuest XT6 around $450

The full-size 6-inch Dobsonian — the classic 'most telescope for the money' at this price.

The classic 6-inch Dobsonian — decades of beginners can't be wrong.

  • Watch out:
  • Long tube needs car transport
  • No tracking
Read the full pick →

#6

Celestron StarSense Explorer DX 130AZ around $480

Your phone plate-solves the sky and guides you to 100+ targets. Training wheels that actually teach you the constellations.

Your phone guides you to 100+ targets.

  • Watch out:
  • Phone mount adds fiddliness
  • 130mm won't resolve fine planetary detail
Read the full pick →
